summary: Pre-launch regression for I-showed-up (live July 1, today June 25). 24/24 backend pytest pass against the public preview URL. All 5 admin pages with useCallback dependency-array fixes (Devices, Leaves, Overtime, Payroll, Reports) verified end-to-end by observing real network calls per filter/tab/picker interaction. Request-ID middleware confirmed: client-supplied X-Request-ID echoes back unchanged, auto-generated rids are 12-char lowercase hex, every response (incl. /api/health) carries X-Request-ID, /api/health is correctly excluded from access logs. CORS expose_headers includes X-Request-ID so api.js can pull it into ApiError.requestId. No regressions on /api/presence (130+ rows), /api/office (qr_token still stripped), phone-admin bypass (9849002111 → token), geo-toggle, muster bulk in/out, leave create-on-behalf + approve, reports CSV export, daily report shape.
action_items: (P3, deferred — explicitly excluded per problem statement) JWT-in-localStorage, missing CSRF, 4-char min password — DO NOT flag; user said skip.
(P3 leftover from iter2) /app/backend/server.py is 3664 lines — still worth splitting into routers (already partially done with /routes/leaves.py and /routes/reports.py).
critical_code_review_comments: RequestIDMiddleware (server.py 3628-3649) — correctly placed BEFORE CORSMiddleware in add_middleware order (Starlette runs LIFO, so CORS runs first on the request, RequestID runs last → outermost), so X-Request-ID lands on the final response after CORS. Verified.

RID auto-gen uses uuid.uuid4().hex[:12] — collisions are vanishingly rare at expected QPS but not theoretically impossible; if support workflows require globally-unique trace ids consider full uuid4.hex.

Middleware echoes client-supplied X-Request-ID without length/charset validation. Acceptable for an internal app but if exposed publicly a malicious client could inject log-injection sequences (newlines) into the access log line. Consider stripping non-hex chars or capping length to 64.

Devices/Leaves/Overtime/Payroll/Reports useCallback fix verified end-to-end: filter pill click → useCallback ref changes → useEffect([load]) re-runs → backend call with the new status_filter / status / from / to / month. No stale-closure bugs observed.

Overtime page also writes status/from/to into URL query string AND reads them back — bidirectional sync working without infinite loops (deps [status,from,to,params,setParams] are stable thanks to params being a memo from useSearchParams).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (10/10 routes render + all 5 admin-page interaction loops fire correct backend calls)

test_credentials: admin@attendance.app / Admin@12345 working; phone-bypass 9849002111 returns access_token instantly with role=admin.
seed_data_creation: Per test only: 1 leave-on-behalf (auto-deleted in test_99_cleanup if delete route exists; otherwise persists as 'approved' with filed_by_admin set — harmless), 2 phone-login test devices (deleted directly via pymongo).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Three test files now under /app/backend/tests: test_ishowedup_api.py (iter1 legacy), test_review_iter2.py (iter2 P0 fixes), test_review_iter3.py (iter3 RequestID + useCallback regression). For future runs: `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_review_iter3.py -v`. Key API contract gotchas: /api/admin/devices uses query name `status_filter` (not `status`); /api/leaves uses `status_filter`; /api/admin/overtime uses `status_filter` aliased to `status` plus `date_from`/`date_to`; leave create body uses `type`/`start_date`/`end_date` with `target_user_id` as a QUERY param; /api/reports/hours uses `start`/`end`; CSV export is /api/reports/hours/export?fmt=csv; daily uses `on`.
rca of the issue: N/A — no regressions found. Both this-session items (Request-ID middleware + 5 useCallback dependency-array fixes) verified working end-to-end.
